questions.text:
import { n } from 'data:text/javascript,export const n = 1';
console.log(n);

import n from 'data:text/javascript,export default 2';
console.log(n);

import { n as m } from 'data:text/javascript,export const n = 3';
console.log(m);

import * as ns from 'data:text/javascript,export const n = 4';
console.log(ns.n);

var n = 1;
console.log(typeof globalThis.n === 'undefined' ? 1 : 0);

console.log(n);
import { n } from 'data:text/javascript,export const n = 7';

import { m } from 'data:text/javascript,const n = 8; export { n as m }';
console.log(m);
Where can static import and export be declared?
options: Only at the top level of a module. Inside a function, if, or block they are a syntax error
Inside any function, as long as that function is not nested
Only on the first line of the file
Anywhere a function can be called

questions.text: How many default exports can one module have?
options: As many as it has named exports
At most one. Named exports can be many
Exactly one: a module without default is invalid
None. default belongs in a separate file

questions.text: What is the specifier of a static import?
options: Any expression. It is evaluated when execution reaches that line
The name of a local variable in this file
A string literal. The module graph is built from it before the body runs

questions.text: What is import './side.mjs' without a binding list for?
options: To copy its variables onto the global object
To wait until the file changes on disk
To evaluate the module for side effects. Importing the same URL again does not run the body

questions.text: One module can export a default and named bindings at the same time.
A static import inside if loads the module only when that branch runs.
The name in import value from must match a variable name in the exporting file.
Module code runs in strict mode.
What is the namespace object property that holds export default?
questions.answer: default. Named exports sit under their own names.

questions.text: What does import(specifier) return?
questions.answer: A promise. On success the value is the module namespace object, not one export.

questions.text: What is a specifier that starts with ./ or ../ resolved against?
questions.answer: The URL of the current module, not the process working directory.

questions.text: Which prefixes make a specifier relative?
questions.answer: ./ and ../. A name without one of those is a bare specifier, resolved by the host.
